doc.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021

title: Dreams, Boston anniversary and goodbye
summary: Closing talk about dreams, the New England Conservatory anniversary, recomposing, and thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: There’s a great deal to learn from you and I think — I don’t have people talking about some of these things, so this has been very valuable for me.
You came up with some wonderful questions and thoughts.

Thank you. If you were to play something, I’m trying to think of the connection between your composing and your 80-some years of memories. Do you have memories that come to you, I mean I know that you had said something about trying to affect the way you dream.

Yes. And one time there was so much disease, racism, everything going on that I said I want to go into an elegant drawing room and have a Agatha Christie mystery where the murdered person is really a terrible person, so there’s no guilt about somebody’s death. I’ve tried that three or four times in the winter and only one time was I successful, but I have a lot of nightmares. I really like to be alone in my room because sometimes it can be noisy with some of my reflections.
Yeah. Well you certainly have made an impact on a lot of people, and I thank you for that. I also am appreciative of how quiet your cat was during the interview.

He usually is more visible and I hope you’ll sometime visit Brookline, Massachusetts or the Conservatory in Boston because we’re celebrating our fiftieth anniversary next year. So people from the past, people there, and we have a marvelous jazz chairperson, Ken Schaphorst who does beautiful arrangements. And I continue still — I call what I do when I think of models — “recomposing” because I add myself but I still want to allude to, I want to allude to somebody else. You’re a great listener, Monk. You have been on all your interviews.
Thank you. I take that as a high compliment. So I’m going to pause our recording here and then we’ll have our official good-bye, all right?
